verses.text: King Darius gave the order, and the archives where Babylon kept its treasures were searched.
A scroll was found at Achmetha in the palace in the province of Media. It contained this record:

"In his first year as king, Cyrus issued this decree about God's house in Jerusalem: Rebuild the house as a place where sacrifices are offered. Lay a strong foundation. The building is to be sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide,
with three rows of large stones and one row of new timber. The royal treasury is to pay the costs.
Return the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem to Babylon. Put them back in their places in God's house in Jerusalem."
So now, Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and your Apharsachite associates in that province, keep away from the site.
Leave the work on God's house alone. Let the Jewish governor and elders rebuild it on its original site.

I also decree what you must do for these Jewish elders as they rebuild God's house: pay their expenses promptly and in full from the royal revenue collected in the province Beyond the River, so the work can go ahead without delay.
Give them whatever the priests in Jerusalem ask for: bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and oil. Provide it every day without fail,
so they can offer sacrifices with a pleasing aroma to the God of heaven and pray for the lives of the king and his sons.

I also decree that if anyone changes this order, a beam is to be pulled from that person's house and the person lifted up and fastened to it. Their house is to be made a pile of refuse for this offense.
May the God who has put his name there overthrow any king or people who would change this decree and destroy God's house in Jerusalem. I, Darius, issue this decree. Carry it out promptly.
Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and their associates promptly did what King Darius had ordered.

The Jewish elders made good progress with the building, encouraged by the words of the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished building it according to the command of the God of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
The house was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of King Darius's reign.
The Israelites, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the returned exiles celebrated the dedication of God's house with joy.
For the dedication they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs, as well as twelve male goats as a sin offering for all Israel, one for each tribe.
They organized the priests by division and the Levites by their assigned groups to serve God in Jerusalem, as written in the Book of Moses.
The returned exiles celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
The priests and Levites had purified themselves together, so they were all clean. The Levites slaughtered the Passover animals for the returned exiles, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.

The Israelites who had returned from exile ate the meal, along with everyone who had joined them and turned away from the unclean practices of the surrounding nations to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.

They celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with joy. The LORD had made them glad by turning the heart of the king of Assyria toward them so that he supported their work on the house of God, the God of Israel.
